facts.evidence: The Firm reported net revenues of $21.3 billion for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared with $16.8 billion a year ago. (headline: "Morgan Stanley Delivers Record Second Quarter Revenues")
Net income applicable to Morgan Stanley was $5.6 billion, or $3.46 per diluted share, versus $3.5 billion, or $2.13 per diluted share, for the same period last year.
Institutional Securities generated record net revenues of $11.0 billion (prior-year $7.6 billion comparative not given)
Return on tangible common equity was 26.6% (prior-year 18.2% and non-GAAP label not given)
Equity net revenues reached a record level with a 69% increase from a year ago (dollar figure of $6,300 million not given)
Wealth Management delivered record net revenues of $8.9 billion (30.5% pre-tax margin not given)
added net new assets of $148 billion for the quarter (the "record" designation and the caveat that just over half came from Workplace-client IPO inflows are not given)
declared a quarterly dividend of $1.15 per share (the 15-cent increase and August 14, 2026 payable date are not given)
The Standardized Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio was 14.8% (prior-year 15.0% comparative not given)

claims.claim: The Firm reported net revenues of $21.3 billion for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026.
Net revenues were $16.8 billion in the prior-year quarter.
Net income applicable to Morgan Stanley was $5.6 billion.
Earnings were $3.46 per diluted share in the quarter.
Prior-year quarter net income applicable to Morgan Stanley was $3.5 billion.
Prior-year quarter earnings were $2.13 per diluted share.
Return on tangible common equity was 26.6%.
The expense efficiency ratio stood at 65% for the first half of the year.
The Firm repurchased $1.5 billion of its outstanding common stock during the quarter.
The Firm declared a quarterly dividend of $1.15 per share.
Institutional Securities generated record net revenues of $11.0 billion.
Investment Banking revenues increased 58% from a year ago.
The Institutional Securities record was driven by the 58% increase in Investment Banking revenues.
claims.note: The release attributes the record to strong performance in Equity (record revenues, up 69%) with Investment Banking cited as an additional source of strength, not as the driver.

claims.claim: The Investment Banking increase was due to higher completed M&A transactions and advisory activity.
claims.note: The release attributes the Investment Banking increase to advisory (higher completed M&A), equity underwriting (higher IPOs, follow-ons, convertibles) and fixed income underwriting alike; crediting it to M&A/advisory alone is not what the release states.

claims.claim: Equity net revenues were a record.
Equity net revenues increased 69% from a year ago.
The Equity result was supported by strong client engagement and favorable market conditions across regions, including Asia.
Wealth Management delivered record net revenues of $8.9 billion.
Wealth Management added net new assets of $148 billion for the quarter.
Wealth Management total client assets reached the $10 trillion milestone.
claims.note: The release states total client assets reached $10 trillion across Wealth Management and Investment Management combined, not Wealth Management alone.

claims.claim: Investment Management reported net revenues of $1.6 billion.
Investment Management revenues were primarily driven by asset management fees on higher average AUM.
Investment Management had positive long-term net flows of $7.5 billion in the quarter.
The release does not provide specific numerical guidance for future quarters or full-year targets.
Management noted that active markets and consistent execution across all three regions drove exceptional results.
This suggests continued momentum in Institutional Securities.
claims.note: Forward-looking inference by the analyst; the release's reference to 'continued momentum in Investment Banking and Fixed Income' describes the reported quarter and makes no statement about future momentum.

claims.claim: The Firm stated it continues to accrete capital, providing incremental flexibility to invest in core businesses while generating strong returns for shareholders.
The Standardized Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio was 14.8%.
The Advanced Approach CET1 capital ratio was 16.2%.
The Tier 1 leverage ratio was 6.0%.
The supplementary leverage ratio (SLR) was 4.9%.
The effective tax rate for the current quarter was 23.1%.
The effective tax rate reflected a slight increase from the prior-year period.
Institutional Securities Other net revenues decreased from a year ago primarily due to higher mark-to-market losses on corporate loans, inclusive of hedges.
Fixed Income results reflected higher results in Credit driven by credit corporates and the cumulative impact of consistent lending growth in the securitized products business.

Under the deferred cash-based compensation (DCP) transition, hedge fair value changes are now recorded in compensation expense or other comprehensive income, and the Firm no longer excludes DCP through non-GAAP measures.
